one_line: Young Emperor Akbar facing Rajput commanders Jaimal and Patta at the siege of Chittorgarh in 16th‑century Rajasthan.

appearance.age_look: Akbar appears about 25, lean but regal; Jaimal mid‑40s, broad‑shouldered; Patta late‑20s, athletic and slightly shorter.
appearance.face: Akbar has an oval face, light wheat complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed pointed beard and thin moustache, with calm intense eyes and a composed, slightly curious default expression; Jaimal’s face is square with a deeper sun‑browned complexion, thick curved moustache, faint crow’s feet and a stern determined gaze; Patta has a slightly angular face, medium wheat complexion, strong jaw, straight nose, bold upward moustache and a spirited, focused expression.
appearance.hair: Akbar’s hair is black, cut short and mostly hidden under a high, rounded Mughal turban of emerald green silk with narrow gold stripes, a white sarpech plume and a central red gem; Jaimal’s black hair is tied back in a small knot under a saffron‑orange cotton pagri with a dark red band; Patta’s dark brown hair is similarly tied under a sky‑blue pagri with a white band and small metallic kalgi at the front.
appearance.costume: Akbar wears a long, calf‑length Mughal jama in rich deep green silk crossing left over right, patterned with fine golden floral butis, a broad maroon sash at the waist, slim cream churidar trousers, and soft dark brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; over his shoulders is a light cream shawl with thin green and gold borders; he has a narrow gold belt, simple gold earrings and a single emerald pendant; Jaimal wears traditional Rajput armour over a deep red cotton angarkha: a riveted steel cuirass and lamellar plates on the torso, over a mustard‑yellow cotton kamarband, with off‑white churidar, sturdy brown leather boots, and a short, split mail skirt; his forearms have leather bracers, and he carries a plain steel helmet hanging at his side; Patta wears slightly lighter armour: a sky‑blue angarkha under a fitted steel breastplate with simple etching, a crimson sash at the waist, indigo churidar trousers, brown leather boots, leather bracers, and a modest mail coif pushed back around his neck, all rendered in sturdy cottons and polished but battle‑worn steel.
appearance.signature: Akbar’s signature prop is an ornate, slightly curved Mughal talwar in a dark brown leather scabbard with gold fittings and a jade‑green hilt, held calmly at his side; Jaimal holds a heavy Rajput spear with leaf‑shaped steel head and red tassel near the socket; Patta grips a distinctive Rajput shield (dhal) of dark steel with four brass bosses and a faint sun motif etched in the center.

ref_desc: Young Akbar with emerald green gold‑patterned jama, cream churidar, maroon sash, green‑striped turban and jade‑hilt talwar stands opposite stern armoured Jaimal in saffron turban and spear, and spirited armoured Patta in sky‑blue turban with sun‑motif shield, all in deep green, maroon, saffron, sky blue and steel grey tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of three fixed characters together from 16th‑century Chittorgarh: young Emperor Akbar, Rajput commander Jaimal and Rajput commander Patta. Akbar is lean and regal, light wheat complexion and oval face, with neat pointed beard and thin moustache, calm intense eyes, and short black hair mostly hidden by a high rounded Mughal turban of emerald green silk with narrow gold stripes, a white plume and central red gem; he wears a long calf‑length deep green silk jama crossing left over right, patterned with fine golden floral butis, a broad maroon sash at the waist, slim cream churidar trousers and soft dark brown upturned shoes, plus a light cream shawl with green and gold borders, a narrow gold belt, simple gold earrings and a single emerald pendant, and he holds an ornate slightly curved talwar in a dark brown scabbard with gold fittings and a jade‑green hilt at his side. Beside him, Jaimal has a square sun‑browned face, thick curved moustache and stern gaze, black hair tied back under a saffron‑orange cotton pagri with a dark red band; he wears deep red cotton angarkha under riveted steel cuirass and lamellar torso plates, a mustard‑yellow kamarband, off‑white churidar, sturdy brown leather boots, leather forearm bracers, a short split mail skirt and a plain steel helmet hanging at his side, gripping a heavy Rajput spear with a leaf‑shaped steel head and red tassel. Patta has an angular face, medium wheat complexion, strong jaw, bold upward moustache and spirited focused expression, with dark brown hair tied under a sky‑blue pagri with white band and small metallic kalgi; he wears a sky‑blue angarkha under a fitted etched steel breastplate, a crimson sash, indigo churidar trousers, brown leather boots, leather bracers and a mail coif pushed back around his neck, holding a dark steel Rajput shield with four brass bosses and a faint sun motif. Use rich but restrained colours dominated by deep green, maroon, saffron orange, sky blue and steel grey, and present them in a neutral stance so their faces, hairstyles, garments, armour, and signature weapons read clearly for consistent redrawing.
